about.title: About Me
description: I am a passionate 8th-semester Computer Systems Engineering student at the Instituto Tecnológico de Tijuana (ITT). My vision of technology is not limited to writing code; I seek to understand and master the entire ecosystem, from the base hardware to cloud deployment. This curiosity drove me to design, assemble, and manage my own bare-metal server (homelab), which I use as my personal laboratory to master Fog Computing architectures, Docker orchestration, Linux systems administration, and network security.

I stand out for my capacity for self-directed learning and my focus on "Deep Work", which allows me to immerse myself in solving complex challenges during highly focused sessions. My short- and medium-term professional goal is to consolidate my profile as a DevOps and Full-Stack Engineer, mastering the development of scalable architectures.

Currently, I am actively seeking a Junior-level job opportunity or professional internship where I can contribute my creativity, my problem-solving work ethic, and my adaptability, while continuing to learn from experienced teams to build solutions that generate real impact.

ada_details.title: Project ADA
ada_details.subtitle: AI-Powered Interactive Kiosk — Instituto Tecnológico de Tijuana
ada_details.problem_body: Every semester, hundreds of incoming students at ITT face the same obstacle: spatial disorientation and lack of immediate access to institutional information. Existing solutions — static maps, physical signage, and in-person queries — are slow, dependent on available staff, and inaccessible to students with visual or motor disabilities. ADA was built to solve this: a 24/7 intelligent voice assistant that answers real questions in natural language.
ada_details.solution_body: ADA is an autonomous physical kiosk with a touchscreen and a push-to-talk button. The student presses the button, asks their question out loud, and the system transcribes the audio, understands the semantic intent, and responds with synthesized voice and real-time captions — all in under 8 seconds. Its knowledge base is built from official ITT documents using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), ensuring accurate and up-to-date answers.
ada_details.interpreter_body: ADA implements the paradigm of a dynamic language interpreter: each voice query passes through lexical analysis (Whisper ASR), syntactic analysis (semantic tokenization and chunking), semantic analysis (Llama 3 via Ollama), and immediate response execution. Unlike a compiler, it generates no persistent output — it processes and responds on the fly, resetting its state after 30 seconds of inactivity.
ada_details.architecture_intro: The design decentralizes processing between a lightweight Edge node and a high-capacity Fog node, connected over a local network to minimize latency.
ada_details.edge_desc: The physical brain of the kiosk. Runs the graphical interface in Flutter (compiled for Linux ARM64), captures audio via USB microphone, manages the physical push-to-talk button via GPIO, and plays back synthesized audio responses. It is the sole point of contact with the user.
ada_details.fog_desc: The intelligence engine of the system. Hosts all AI microservices in independent containers: the voice transcriber, the language model, the semantic search engine (RAG), and the voice synthesizer. Communicates with the Edge node via WebSockets over the local network.

pipeline_steps.desc: The user presses the physical button and speaks. Audio is captured in WAV format.
faster-whisper converts audio to text, identifying phonetic tokens in the language.
ChromaDB performs semantic search over ITT documents to retrieve relevant context.
Llama 3 analyzes the user's intent and generates a contextualized response.
PiperTTS converts the text to audio. The UI plays the audio and highlights each word in the subtitles in real time.

kanua_details.title: Kanua Petto
kanua_details.subtitle: Persistent Multi-Device Virtual Pet
kanua_details.description: Kanua Petto is a modern reimagination of the virtual pet. Unlike classic Tamagotchis locked to a single device, Kanua Petto is omnipresent: its existence persists in the cloud and travels instantly between your PC and your phone. You can feed it while studying at your computer, and seconds later continue playing with it on your phone on the bus. It breaks the device barrier to create a true and continuous companionship experience.

features.name: Cloud Synchronization
features.desc: The pet's full state (hunger, happiness, health, inventory) is saved in MongoDB and synced automatically between PC and Android via the REST API with JWT authentication.

features.name: Personality / Affinity System
features.desc: The pet is not a static robot. Its mood changes based on how it's treated over time. Consistent care unlocks a loving personality, while neglect makes it grumpy and distant.

features.name: Cultural Gastronomy
features.desc: The shop integrates relatable cultural foods: from Chocolate Milk and Croissants to Tamales, Burritos, and Tacos. Too much Maruchan negatively affects the pet's health.

features.name: Ludic Economy (Tic-Tac-Toe)
features.desc: Coins don't fall from the sky. Players earn them by facing the AI in classic Tic-Tac-Toe. Each victory grants coins and increases the companion's happiness.

kanua_details.architecture_intro: The system is split into two major layers: the native game client and the cloud server, orchestrated with Docker Compose.

architecture_items.name: Client — Godot 4.5 / C#
architecture_items.desc: The game runs natively on PC (Windows) and Android, compiled with Godot Engine 4.5 and C# (.NET) scripting. It communicates with the REST API to load and sync the pet's state each session.

architecture_items.name: REST API — Node.js / Express
architecture_items.desc: Express 4.18 backend exposing endpoints for registration, login, state sync, and loading. Passwords are hashed with bcryptjs and sessions are managed via JWT tokens (jsonwebtoken 9).

architecture_items.name: Database — MongoDB / Mongoose
architecture_items.desc: NoSQL persistence via MongoDB with Mongoose 7.0 as ODM. The User model stores the full petState: hunger, happiness, health, coins, inventory (Map), and affinity, plus a lastSync timestamp.

architecture_items.name: Infrastructure — Docker Compose + Cloudflare
architecture_items.desc: Three orchestrated services: mongo_db (persistent volume), api (Node:18 Alpine, port 3005), and tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel to kp.stellarbanana.com). No public IP required.

roadmap_items.desc: Cloud sync PC↔Android, affinity/personality system, ludic economy with Tic-Tac-Toe, shop with cultural gastronomy.
Adaptive AI Engine: algorithms that analyze interaction patterns to shape a unique, evolving personality per user.
Creation Studio: desktop tool to design, import, and modify custom sprites. Online Community Hub to share creations.
Dedicated Physical Device: connected Tamagotchi-style hardware that takes the experience off mobile, with full cloud sync.

kanua_details.justification: The fragmentation of today's digital experiences prevents the formation of deep emotional bonds with technology. Each game or app traps user progress on a single platform, breaking continuity when switching devices. Kanua Petto was built to close this gap: an omnipresent companion that combats digital loneliness, fosters emotional well-being, and opens a creative platform for artists and designers.

functional_items.name: Account Management

functional_items.name: Persistent Life

functional_items.name: Cross-Platform Sync

functional_items.name: Economy & Inventory

functional_items.name: Dynamic Personality

about_details.title: Get to Know Me Better
story: My name is Brian Guadalupe Tellez Escobar, and I am a passionate Computer Systems Engineering student. My technological story began driven by a genuine curiosity: I have never settled for just knowing how to use things, I always want to understand how they work from the inside out.

This same curiosity led me to build my own Homelab. What started as a simple hobby setting up dedicated servers to play with my friends (Minecraft, Terraria), quickly escalated into my own cloud architecture laboratory. Through intensive self-learning, I immersed myself in Linux systems administration, leaving the comfort of the GUI to master the command line, manage local networks, and expose services securely with Cloudflare tunnels.

To me, programming has never been an academic obligation or a work burden. I see it purely as the ultimate medium to bring my ideas to life. If I can imagine a system, a platform, or a solution, code is simply the brick I use to build it.
